title: SMC Production Incident – Project Execution Stuck Due to High Log/Data Storage
description:
Multiple projects running in the SMC Production environment entered a stuck execution state.

The issue was initially identified when Health Check alerts were triggered because the Health Check project, which continuously reports production metrics, also became stuck. As a result, no monitoring metrics were generated, indicating a broader issue affecting project execution.

During the investigation, it was observed that several project messages remained in a pending state and were no longer being processed.

To restore normal production processing, the affected projects were redeployed, additional projects that were in a stuck execution state were restarted, and project execution resumed successfully.

comments.author: Babai Chatterjee
comments.detail: This issue is temporararily resolved by redeploying affected projects.

rca:
To identify the cause of the issue, the following investigation activities were performed:
•	Verified the pending messages for the affected projects. 
•	Reviewed the execution status of running projects. 
•	Analyzed project storage utilization under the production project directory. 
•	Performed filesystem utilization analysis using df -h. 
•	Performed project-level storage analysis using du -sh. 
•	Conducted folder-level analysis for projects consuming high disk space.

Filesystem	Total Size	Used	Available	Usage
/dev/nvme0n1p1	200 GB	99 GB	101 GB	50%

Observation
The production server had approximately 101 GB of available disk space. Therefore, the issue was not caused by overall server disk exhaustion.
Project-level storage analysis identified the following storage utilization:
•	MX_Peru: 38 GB – The logs directory alone occupied approximately 38 GB, while the other folders were relatively small. 
•	MX_Bolivia: 30 GB – Large storage consumption was observed primarily within the project logs. 
•	MX_Colombia: 16 GB. 
•	Netherlands: 8 GB. 
•	Brazil: 3.9 GB – The data directory consumed more than 1 GB of storage. 
•	Other projects: Less than 1 GB each. 

These observations indicate that a significant amount of storage was being consumed by project-generated logs and accumulated project data.
resolution:
To restore normal production processing, the following actions were performed:

•	Redeployed the following projects: 
o	MX_Peru 
o	MX_Bolivia 
o	Brazil 

•	Restarted additional projects that were in a stuck execution state. 

•	Verified that project execution resumed successfully after redeployment and restarts. 
          These actions resolved the issue temporarily and allowed production processing to continue.
